extracted.intended_audience: general readers of entertainment news; fans and practitioners of sketch/political comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and practical criteria for creating political satire and impersonations on a sketch-comedy show (exemplified by Tina Fey's work on SNL). Focuses on truthfulness, tone, context sensitivity, and collaborative writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair hit (grounded in truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We always worked really hard to make sure that we felt like they were what we would call 'a fair hit.' It only felt like it would work if it was based in something that was true."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire and impersonations should be rooted in verifiable or recognizable traits/behaviors of the target; aim for fairness by basing jokes on real facts or widely observed characteristics so the bit 'works' and feels justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth as prerequisite for humor
rubrics_metrics.description: "If it's not true, it will not be funny."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inventing false claims or distortions as the basis for jokes; comedic effectiveness depends on a perceivable connection between the joke and reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance absurdity with astuteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fey emphasized "striking the right balance between absurd and astute" while portraying a public figure like Palin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine exaggerated or absurd elements with sharp, observant points about the target — too absurd without insight can fall flat, while too literal may lack comedic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context sensitivity and changing norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Fey conceded that "not all my bits had aged well" and acknowledged being "on the wrong side of that" for some jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that jokes can age poorly as social norms and historical perspective change; periodically reassess past material and be willing to regret or retire bits that no longer align with current values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of real-world consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: "The show’s relationship to current events became a thinner and thinner veil... something you say will be heard by the person in charge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that satire can be noticed directly by political figures and may have reputational or cultural consequences; consider how visibility changes the stakes of a joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume satire controls politics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does 'SNL' try to control the narrative and politics?' And they really do not. And also, you really can’t."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach political satire as commentary rather than a tool for steering political outcomes; do not craft material under the assumption that it will decisively change public opinion or narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative crafting with writing partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Fey described crafting the GOP caricature "with writing partners Amy Poehler and Seth Meyers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use collaborative writing and performance input to refine impersonations — multiple perspectives help ensure accuracy, fairness, and sharper comedic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible sharpness: 'ruthless' but fair impersonation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fey called her impersonation of Sarah Palin a "fair hit" and it was described as a "ruthless impersonation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impersonations can be incisive or ruthless in tone, but should retain a fairness rooted in truth to avoid gratuitous or unfair personal attacks; sharpness is acceptable when defensible.
